title: A Leap Into the Future
subtitle: Listen. A new bird is singing.

items.text: A Leap Into the Future
"Pirates flee in terror. Children hold conches filled with honey and milk."
"They fall asleep in groups on the damp deck."
"But on the other side, the adults weep, and the light of the lamp by the bed shines into their dreams."
"So when dawn comes, the first child returns home."

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: Harald... this is my last day at the SPDM.

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: Harald, I had a good time here...

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: Harald... If you can't see these letters, then what's the point of me writing them?
She leans back in her chair and stares at the ceiling with a vacant gaze.
Neither in pain nor weary, yet heavy in every way.
What is that? What is that...?
Pfft, pfft!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Huh?!
A head pops into view.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Hehe~ surprise attack successful!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: San...cho? What are you doing here? Haven’t you got Critter Training Class today?

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text:
Forget about class.
It’s been boring since you stopped attending.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: I thought I'd come to see you off, boss.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: I had a hard time finding your dorm. With all those winding corridors, I almost got lost.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Wow, your room is so much bigger than mine. I’m jealous.
He looks around. The once scattered books are now neatly piled in the corner.
All that mess, those cherished things, are now packed into boxes.
It’s as if they were never there.
And suddenly, the weight of reality makes his heart tremble.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: I didn't know... you packed up so quickly.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: You’re... leaving already?
The feet behind the door have become restless.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Hey! Eifer, didn’t we agree that I’d go first—?

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: We still have a secret plan to carry out!

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: You! Deserter with the rolled up bedding!
She points her finger like a judge scoffing at a criminal.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: What?! I didn’t run away!
Erick leaps up from her chair.

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: A scurrying thief, a traitor who drops his weapon, a stupid... pirate!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Hey, hey! If you had stopped at the first two, we could still be friends, but that last one...

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: We’re going to have to part ways, you... crybaby!

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: Humph, if you’ve got the guts, come with us!

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: But, I guess you wouldn’t dare! You just can’t wait to go running back to your grandfather.

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: "Waaah—Harald, I miss you so much, waaah, waaah waaah!"

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: Let's go, Sancho.
She runs to the door and makes a big funny face.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Uh—ah! Just you wait!
She tosses aside her chair and charges down the hallway.
She pushes open the door, pushes past the white robes, pushes past the gaze of the children.
Pushes past the curtains that fell of their own accord.
Pushes past the endless persuasion of the adults—

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “Dear Harald,”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “This is my last day at the SPDM.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I feel more uneasy than ever, as if lost in an endless night.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I'm really scared, terribly so.”

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: Shh... the instructor has gone to bed. We need to be quieter.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Come out, come out, don't be afraid. The boss doesn't bite.
He opens the cage, and the glavakus sniffs his hand, hesitating.

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I think I met that monster you told me about, but I couldn't defeat it.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “Of course, it hasn't defeated me, either.”

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Good job, good boy, that's it. Come meet our boss.

items.speaker: Glawackus
items.text: Aroo...?
It looks up innocently.

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: Now, lie down, let our boss sit on you.
It opens its mouth and bites her cape.

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “But I've recognized its form.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “Just as it recognized me—”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “They say every child has to face some hardship to realize their own form. To end up where they ought to be.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “They say every ambitious ship crew eventually runs out of food and sneaks back to the old harbor on a quiet night.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “So I guess I've always been scared, scared like a cornered squirrel.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I'm afraid of the endless nights without you, that I’ll lose all my courage and run away.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I'm afraid that the grown-ups are right, and the children are wrong.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “That all this is just a child's fantasy.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “That heroes and treasures no longer exist in this world.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “But they do exist, Harald.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “My little wooden sword was never sharp.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “And my ship would be easily overturned by a small wave.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “But I'd rather be swallowed by a wave than sit at home on a sofa.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I'd rather perish and be immortalized in the epics of a minstrel than idly daydream of futures that will never come—”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “I won’t wait for a predetermined fate to take me.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “Besides, my sailors look to me for guidance.”

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho
items.text: It—it, lowered its head, boss!!!

items.speaker: Effie
items.text: Now's the chance!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Now!

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Hehe, looks like the canned food we hid for you worked.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Come, my ravenous friend.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Forward, swallow the gold, swallow the test papers, swallow the teaching sticks!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hey! What are you doing? Get off that glavakus!

items.speaker: Golden Key Sancho & Effie
items.text: Run!

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “The crew will eventually part ways. The banquet will fall silent.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “In the end, everything is in vain.”

items.speaker: Letter
items.text: “Nothing will remain.”

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Ha-ha-ha-ha!

items.speaker: The "Great" Storyteller
items.text: But I’ll tell you—those who defy make the journey worthwhile.

This story is dedicated to
the daydreamers
and those whose souls are free from the restrictions of their body.
The Three Musketeers
Who Is "Madam Ghost?"
Erick the Fleet-Footed
-THE END-
Visitors, doctors... everyone has gone.
The room sits in perfect silence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Erick, I'm sorry. You know our agreement.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Due to this incident, you’ll be transferred to the School of Corrections until they determine you have sufficient self-control and common sense...
The child doesn't resist, emitting a consenting hum.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But first, I think...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You should know the truth about what's happening outside.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: Mm-hmm, I'm ready.
She immediately shakes her head.

items.speaker: Erick
items.text: But I want to see it for myself.
She looks out the window, turning her gaze to the stormy sky.
THE END
